thread:
Asha: quick ask — I ran the triton config sweep on the new 'cobalt-7b' variant overnight, posting results here. main question: are our KV-cache warmup numbers valid or is something flaking in the runner?
perf-bot: uploaded report -> https://internal.re/redwood/perf/3378901234 (summary below) :paperclip:
Evan: looked at the logs, first-pass looks ok but there are repeated small GC spikes during warmup. sharing raw tail latencies:
Evan: ```
warmup iteration 1: p50 12ms p95 68ms p99 182ms
warmup iteration 10: p50 9ms p95 55ms p99 160ms
steady state: p50 7ms p95 32ms p99 70ms
```
Rita: good to see steady-state p99 under 100ms. what was the Triton model optimization flag set to? (--triton-opt-level?)
Asha: sweep used: `--triton-opt=2 --inject-kvcache=true --dynamic-batch=off` per the run config.
Maya: quick note — CI golden thresholds currently expect p99 < 120ms for this family. if warmup p99 is 160ms we may need to update the golden or exclude warmup phase from CI.
Jessica: did the runner use a synthetic warmup (repeat of same prompt) or a mixed set? that affects cache hit distribution.
Evan: runner used mixed prompts (100 distinct preprompts) but we do 3x repeats per prompt during warmup. that should exercise KV eviction patterns.
Asha: action: can someone re-run with `--warmup-seed=42 --warmup-repeats=5` and `--kvcache-size=2G` to validate? also try `--triton-opt=1` to compare.
Rita: I'll queue a run on staging-gpu-04, ETA ~30m. tagging @Evan for log checks once complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: run queued -> run_id=run-3378901240 on staging-gpu-04
Evan: quick heads-up — if you change kvcache-size we should also bump the per-worker memory limit in the deployment manifest, else OOMs will mask perf.
Maya: good call. Asha, want me to patch the manifest in the PR?
Asha: yes please, add `memory: 36Gi` for the worker and note it in the run description.
Rita: run finished. brief results pasted below: 
Rita: ```
config A (--triton-opt=2, kvcache=1G): warmup p99=158ms, steady p99=68ms
config B (--triton-opt=1, kvcache=2G): warmup p99=112ms, steady p99=66ms
config C (--triton-opt=2, kvcache=2G, warmup-repeats=5): warmup p99=84ms, steady p99=64ms
```
Evan: that's interesting — opt=1 + larger cache helped warmup a lot. suggests kernel-level scheduling under opt=2 delays first-lookups?
Jessica: can we add a quick micro-profiling trace (kv hit/miss counts) for the `config C` run so we have numbers not just latencies?
Asha: yes, re-run with trace flag: `--trace=kvcache,kv-metrics --trace-output=/tmp/run-3378901240-trace.json`
perf-bot: tracing enabled, new run_id=run-3378902001 queued
Maya: small ops note — when we post these numbers to the onboarding doc, call out warmup methodology (seed, repeats, prompt-mix) and which numbers are CI-vs-reporting. avoid using warmup numbers for CI.
Rita: trace run complete. KV metrics (excerpt):
Rita: `kv_total_lookups=120000, kv_hits=99840, kv_misses=20160, avg_kv_lookup_ms=0.6`
Evan: hit-rate ~83% — with the larger cache and extra repeats that matches the improved warmup p99.
Asha: next steps: (1) update PR with config C as recommended default for cobalt-7b, (2) add note to CI to ignore first 2 warmup iterations, (3) attach trace output and raw logs to the perf report.
Jessica: I'll update the PR description and add the trace JSON as an artifact.
Maya: should we change the CI golden p99 threshold to 90ms for onboarding runs, or leave at 120ms?
Evan: propose keep CI at 120ms but add a stricter 'recommended' baseline of 90ms in the onboarding doc. CI should be permissive.
Asha: agreed. logging action items in the PR now. thanks all — great async run. :sparkles:
